decisions: Fix-request-review-013.md (review cycle 13, major severity) reported computeRatingFacet at typeorm-product.repository.ts:594 loading the full matching-product rating set into application memory (one rating_average row per matching active product via a LATERAL join with LIMIT 1, mapped and filtered per bucket in Node), violating task.md:122's requirement that facet counts be computed in the query/repository without loading the full dataset. Verified the finding was still present in the current worktree code before fixing (grepped the exact lines cited).

Fix: rewrote computeRatingFacet to issue a single bounded aggregate query — COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.rating_average >= $N THEN p.id END)::int per rating bucket — using the same effectiveVariantLateralSql 'has an effective variant matching every other active filter' guard the original code already applied, so rating self-exclusion (exclude:'rating' in buildConditions) and every other active price/prep/rush/catalog filter are preserved exactly as before. This mirrors computeBucketFacet's existing price/preparation/rush pattern (same file, ~line 513) rather than inventing a new shape.

Extended the fix request's cited gap directly: products.e2e-spec.ts's large multi-variant regression test (24-variant fixture) previously only asserted 3 bounded aggregate queries (price/preparation/rush, identified by the SQL substring 'COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN'). Since rating now uses the identical SQL shape, updated the assertion to expect 4 bounded aggregate queries, each still returning exactly one row — this is the 'SQL/integration regression proving the rating facet is counted by a bounded database aggregate' the fix request explicitly asked for.
